November 26, 2026 – TheNewswire - Montreal, Quebec, Canada - Beauce Gold Fields (“Champs d’Or en Beauce”) (TSX Venture: BGF), referred to as “BGF” or the “Company,” is pleased to announce that sonic drilling has commenced on the Delery and Chaussegros Sections of the Saint-Simon-les-Mines paleoplacer gold channel in southern Quebec.

The Company plans to complete approximately 20 sonic drill holes, with additional holes to be completed depending on ground conditions, drilling productivity, saprolite thickness and the time required to advance each hole.
Click Image To View Full Size
Image: Sonic Drilling Paleoplacer Channel

The majority of the program will be concentrated within the Delery Section, at the western end of the nearly six-kilometre-long paleoplacer channel. Four additional sonic drill holes are planned in the Chaussegros Section, where geological interpretation indicates that an ancient tributary may have entered the northern flank of the Gilbert River paleovalley.

The program is designed to test auriferous basal sedimentary horizons, saprolitic and fractured bedrock, as well as interpreted tributary, confluence and deltaic features within the paleovalley. Selected historical drill locations will also be tested or twinned to compare modern sonic drilling results with historical geological data and to better evaluate local gold-grade variability in a coarse-gold system characterized by a pronounced nugget effect.
Patrick Levasseur, President and CEO of Beauce Gold Fields, commented:

“We are very excited to have the sonic drill turning at Saint-Simon-les-Mines. We are now drilling directly into unmined portions of this historic placer gold deposit using modern sonic methods to test its gold potential and the geological basis of our current Exploration Target. Historical mining demonstrated that this system hosts significant coarse gold, while subsequent drilling and geological work indicate that the paleoplacer may be more extensive than previously understood. This program gives us the opportunity to directly test both the historical gold-bearing channel and geological features that may have played an important role in concentrating gold.”
Delery and Chaussegros Drill Program

The Delery Section represents the principal focus of the current sonic drilling program. The sector is interpreted to have been fed by the Giroux Brook tributary, one of the most important tributaries entering the northern flank of the Gilbert River paleovalley and an area historically worked for placer gold during the 19th century.

The Chaussegros Section will be tested by four sonic drill holes. Geological interpretation indicates that this portion of the paleovalley may have been fed by an ancient tributary entering from the north, making it a priority target for testing potential tributary-related gold accumulation.

In both the Delery and Chaussegros Sections, the current sonic drilling will test areas previously drilled by Beauce Placer Mining Company in 1959 and Coniagas Mines in 1985. In the Delery Section, the program will test the area of the L16+500 historical drill line completed by Beauce Placer Mining Company and the G-49 and G-50 drill lines completed by Coniagas. In the Chaussegros Section, drilling will test historical Beauce Placer Mining Company holes as well as the G-57 drill line completed by Coniagas. One additional Chaussegros hole is planned near a 1985 Geological Survey of Canada drill hole.

The sonic drilling method is particularly suited to the program because it provides relatively continuous recovery through unconsolidated sediments, saprolite and weathered bedrock, while allowing larger-volume samples to be collected from a deposit characterized by coarse gold and a pronounced nugget effect.
Subject to results and available financing, the Company plans to continue testing additional sections of the channel during 2027.
Five Paleoplacer Sections

For exploration purposes, BGF has subdivided the Saint-Simon-les-Mines paleoplacer channel into five principal sections, each corresponding to an area where a current or interpreted ancient tributary entered the paleovalley from its northern flank:
Delery Section, including the Giroux Brook tributary, historically worked during the 19th century;
Chaussegros Section, where an interpreted ancient tributary entered the paleovalley near Rang Chaussegros;
Saint-Gustave Section, located near Rang Saint-Gustave and the area historically worked by Yuba dredge operations during the 1960s;
G80–G85 Section, where previous exploration identified an interpreted tributary-related deltaic target; and
Rang 6 Section, located at the eastern end of the paleovalley near the headwaters of the Gilbert River.

Image: Polygonal – Longitudinal Map of the Saint-Simon-les-Mines Paleoplacer Channel
About the Saint-Simon-les-Mines Paleoplacer Channel

The Saint-Simon-les-Mines paleoplacer is a nearly six-kilometre-long buried gold-bearing channel within the Gilbert River paleovalley and represents the core of Canada’s first gold rush district. Historical mining from the 1860s through the 1960s recovered significant quantities of coarse gold, including multi-ounce nuggets.

The Company’s geological model indicates that gold mineralization within the paleoplacer system is concentrated principally within basal sedimentary horizons, saprolitic bedrock and fractures or natural traps developed along the paleovalley floor.

The paleovalley lies immediately south of the Company’s interpreted Saddle Reef-style antiform structures. BGF’s geological model is evaluating these structures and associated quartz-vein systems as potential bedrock sources for at least part of the historical placer gold.

Historical and modern geological work also indicates that tributaries entering the Gilbert River paleovalley from the north may have played an important role in transporting and concentrating gold. Interpreted deltaic deposits developed at tributary mouths therefore represent priority exploration targets for the sonic drilling program.

Exploration Target
The drilling program follows the Company’s June 2026 technical assessment of the Saint-Simon-les-Mines paleoplacer channel, which established an Exploration Target ranging between:
4,004,674 and 5,991,229 cubic metres; and
2.02 g Au/m³ to 12.0 g Au/m³

The Exploration Target is based on the interpretation of historical drilling, geological modelling and reconstruction of the Gilbert River paleovalley, polygonal volumetric calculations, and the evaluation of auriferous basal sedimentary, saprolitic and weathered bedrock units.

The updated geological interpretation recognizes the potential importance of buried tributaries and deltaic deposits, natural bedrock traps and greater-than-previously-recognized thicknesses of saprolitic and fractured bedrock within the paleovalley.

The potential quantity and grade of the Exploration Target are conceptual in nature. There has been insufficient exploration to define a mineral resource, and it is uncertain whether further exploration will result in the delineation of a mineral resource.
Jean Bernard, B.Sc., P.Geo., an independent Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101, has reviewed and approved the technical content of this news release.
About Beauce Gold Fields

Beauce Gold Fields is focused on exploring and developing the historic placer gold district of the Beauce region of southern Quebec. The Company’s objective is to trace historical placer gold workings back to potential bedrock sources and evaluate the potential for economic lode-gold mineralization.

The Company’s flagship property is the Saint-Simon-les-Mines gold project, site of Canada’s first gold rush, which predates the Yukon Klondike. The Beauce region hosted major historical placer gold operations from the 1860s through the 1960s and produced some of the largest gold nuggets recorded in Canadian mining history, including nuggets exceeding 50 ounces. (Source: SEDAR, NI 43-101 Report – Beauce, July 4, 2018, author B. Violette.)

Beauce Gold Fields continues to explore antiform structures that the Company believes may have contributed gold to the extensive auriferous placer deposits of the Beauce region. The Company’s geological model is evaluating whether structural traps associated with antiform folding and saddle-reef-style quartz mineralization may represent potential bedrock sources for gold found within the historical Beauce paleoplacer system.
